direct_item_inputs.interface_excerpt: Use the lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, the finite spin dimension $q\ge1$, the local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z=\max_{x,y\in Z}d_\infty(x,y)$; for finite nonempty $X,Y\subset\Gamma$, write $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(X,Y)=\min_{x\in X,y\in Y}d_\infty(x,y)$. A **uniformly bounded finite-range interaction** is a family $\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_Z$, indexed by finite nonempty $Z\subset\Gamma$, such that $\Phi(Z)^*=\Phi(Z)$ and there are an integer $M\ge1$, a finite $R\ge0$, and $\kappa<\infty$ satisfying $$\Phi(Z)=0\quad\text{if }|Z|>M\text{ or }\operatorname{diam}_\infty Z>R,\qquad\kappa:=\sup_{x\in\Gamma}\sum_{Z\ni x}\|\Phi(Z)\|<\infty.$$ The norm in this sum is the operator norm in the local matrix algebra $\mathcal A_Z$. If a model lists several terms with the same support, first add them in that local algebra; the resulting single operator is $\Phi(Z)$, and $\kappa$ uses its norm. Thus no multiplicity is implicit. For a finite region $\Lambda\subset\Gamma$, define the **free-boundary finite-volume Hamiltonian** by summing only terms whose complete support lies inside $\Lambda$; terms meeting $\Lambda$ but extending outside it are omitted: $$H_\Lambda:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne Z\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi(Z)\in\mathcal A_\Lambda.$$ It is a finite sum of self-adjoint matrices. For a fixed scale $\hbar>0$ and any finite $\Omega\supseteq\Lambda$, embed $H_\Lambda$ in $\mathcal A_\Omega$ by the canonical factor inclusion and define $$\alpha_t^\Lambda(A):=e^{itH_\Lambda/\hbar}Ae^{-itH_\Lambda/\hbar}\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Omega,\ t\in\mathbb R).$$ These actions are compatible as $\Omega$ increases, because the extra tensor factors carry the identity. On $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ this is the ordinary finite matrix Heisenberg dynamics. In physical SI bookkeeping, when $\Phi(Z)$ is interpreted as an energy, $\Phi(Z)$, $\kappa$, and $H_\Lambda$ have units J, $t$ has units s, and $\hbar$ is the adopted reduced Planck constant with units J s. The mathematics below uses only $\hbar>0$ and asserts no measured parameter value.

Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in its first argument. An operator $\rho\in\mathcal B(H)$ is a **density operator** when it is positive, trace class, and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Here trace class means compact with summable singular values, and $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the basis-independent trace of a trace-class operator. The **normal density state represented by $\rho$** is the functional on bounded operators $ \omega_\rho(A):=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A),\qquad A\in\mathcal B(H). $ In this page, “normal density state” means this specified trace-pairing representation; no equivalence with other definitions of normal functionals is assumed. The trace pairing is used only for bounded $A$. Unbounded observables are treated through their spectral probability measures in [[lem-qsm-trace-state-calculus]].

Here a complex C$^*$-algebra is a complex Banach algebra with associative bilinear multiplication, submultiplicative norm, and a conjugate-linear involution satisfying $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$; **unital** means that it has a nonzero identity $I$ ([[def-c-star-algebra]]). A $*$-automorphism is a bijective complex-linear map preserving multiplication and involution. Let $t\mapsto\alpha_t$ be a one-parameter group of such automorphisms, so $\alpha_0$ is the identity and $\alpha_s\alpha_t=\alpha_{s+t}$. It is **strongly continuous** when $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for each fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. A **state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ with $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$; this is the state convention of [[def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state]]. Fix absolute temperature $T>0$ in kelvins and Boltzmann's constant $k_B>0$ in J K$^{-1}$; the inverse-temperature parameter is $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}>0$, measured in J$^{-1}$. Let the reduced Planck constant $\hbar>0$ have units J s. Write $b:=\beta\hbar$, measured in seconds, and $$S_b:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\},\qquad S_b^\circ:=\{z\in\mathbb C:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}.$$ A state $\omega$ is a **$\beta$-KMS state for $\alpha$ in physical time** when for every $A,B\in\mathcal A$ there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}:S_b\to\mathbb C$ (that is, $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F_{A,B}(z)|<\infty$) that is continuous on $S_b$, complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and satisfies $$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega\!\left(A\alpha_t(B)\right),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+ib)=\omega\!\left(\alpha_t(B)A\right)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$ For the assigned quantum spin model, $\mathcal A$ is the norm-completed quasi-local algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] and $\alpha$ is the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]], under that theorem's stated hypotheses. The strip width is $\beta\hbar$ in physical seconds; setting $\hbar=1$ is a separate natural-unit convention. This is a mathematical equilibrium criterion for the specified algebra and dynamics. It does not assert that a model describes a material, that a system has dynamically relaxed, or that all stationary states are KMS.

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the triangle inequality follows from $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$. For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis. For $\Lambda=\varnothing$, $S_\Lambda$ is a singleton and $\mathcal H_\Lambda\cong\mathbb C$. The **local spin matrix algebra** is $$\mathcal A_\Lambda:=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)\cong M_{q^{|\Lambda|}}(\mathbb C),$$ Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional Hilbert space; they are bounded. The algebra has composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity $I_\Lambda$, and induced operator norm $$\|T\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|T\xi\|.$$ The **finite local trace** is $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(T):=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}\langle T e_s,e_s\rangle$ in the displayed configuration basis $(e_s)$. This is the usual finite-matrix trace; basis independence and its cyclic/unitary identities are supplied by [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]]. If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, restriction of configurations gives the canonical factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$, with sites ordered lexicographically. The **factor inclusion** is the unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$ given by $T\mapsto T\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. A **localization region** for $T$ is any finite $\Lambda$ for which $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ under these inclusions; a localization region need not be minimal. The ordinary operator norm makes each local matrix algebra a nonzero unital complete C*-algebra, and every positive normalized complex-linear functional is uniquely a trace pairing with a density matrix, by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. This includes the empty region, whose Hilbert space is $\mathbb C$. This definition does not posit an infinite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert space.

Use the finite local matrix algebras and isometric factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric]]. Identify $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ with its image in every larger finite-region algebra. The directed union $$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$$ is the algebra of **strictly local observables**. Its norm is $\|A\|=\|A\|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ for any finite localization region $\Lambda$ of $A$; isometric inclusions make this independent of the chosen region. The **quasi-local spin algebra** is the norm completion $$\mathcal A:=\overline{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.$$ The C*-algebra structure on this completion has product and adjoint extended continuously from the finite local matrix algebras. Countable Choice is assumed for the published existence theorem for metric completions; [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]] supplies the full extension argument using the finite C*-identity of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. **No global Hilbert tensor product is selected.** “Quasi-local” means norm completion of the directed algebra of finite-region observables; it does not mean a chosen representation as operators on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space. A local operator $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ may have more than one localization region. Disjoint finite local factors commute in their common finite tensor algebra.

Assume Countable Choice for the norm completion in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be positive trace-one matrices, one on each finite-region algebra $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], such that for every $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$ their partial traces agree: $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$. There is a unique infinite algebraic state $\omega$ on $\mathcal A$ whose restriction to each $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ is $A\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)$.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, $D=\dim H\ge1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. With composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity and the induced operator norm, $\mathcal B(H)$ is a nonzero unital complex C*-algebra in the sense of [[def-c-star-algebra]]. In particular it is complete, $\|AB\|\le\|A\|\|B\|$, $\|A^*A\|=\|A\|^2$, $\|A^*\|=\|A\|$ and $\|I\|=1$. The matrix $\|A\|^2I-A^*A$ is positive semidefinite and has a positive square root in $\mathcal B(H)$. Every complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal B(H)\to\mathbb C$ that is positive, meaning $\omega(B^*B)\ge0$ for all $B$, has a unique positive semidefinite matrix $\rho$ such that $\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ for all $A$. It is bounded and satisfies $$|\omega(A)|\le\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)\|A\|\quad(A\in\mathcal B(H)),\qquad \|\omega\|=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)=\omega(I).$$ Consequently the canonical states of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]] are exactly the trace pairings of density operators of [[def-qc-density-operator]]; for a positive functional, normalization $\omega(I)=1$ is equivalent to norm one. The result includes zero positive functionals, nonfaithful densities and $D=1$; it makes no infinite-dimensional density representation assertion.

Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, with finite on-site spin dimension $q\ge1$, local matrix algebras $\mathcal A_\Lambda$, and quasi-local algebra $\mathcal A$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction as in [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]], with free-boundary Hamiltonians $H_{\Lambda_n}$ on any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\Gamma$. Fix $\hbar>0$ and $\beta>0$, and let $\alpha_t$ be the thermodynamic dynamics of [[thm-qsm-finite-range-spin-dynamics]]. For each $n$, let $\rho_n=e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}}/\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda_n}(e^{-\beta H_{\Lambda_n}})$ be the finite Gibbs density. For each finite $X\subseteq\Gamma$, define its extension density by adjoining the normalized trace density $q^{-1}I$ at every site of $X\setminus\Lambda_n$ and taking the partial trace from $X\cup\Lambda_n$ to $X$. Assume the finite-matrix C$^*$-identity and the finite-matrix state/density-norm interface recorded in Facts [A1]–[A2]. The resulting consistent local densities define algebraic states $\omega_n$ on $\mathcal A$. At least one subsequence $\omega_{n_k}$ converges pointwise on $\mathcal A$ to an algebraic state $\omega$. For every pointwise-convergent subsequence and its limit $\omega$, and for every fixed pair of strictly local observables $A,B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$, there is a bounded function $F_{A,B}$, continuous on $S_{\beta\hbar}$ and holomorphic inside, whose boundaries are $$F_{A,B}(t)=\omega(A\alpha_t(B)),\qquad F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\omega(\alpha_t(B)A)\quad(t\in\mathbb R).$$ This is the local-pair boundary conclusion for a pointwise limit of finite Gibbs states.

Let $b>0$ and $S_b=\{z\in\mathbb C:0\le\operatorname{Im}z\le b\}$, with interior $S_b^\circ=\{z:0<\operatorname{Im}z<b\}$. Let $F:S_b\to\mathbb C$ be bounded (so $\sup_{z\in S_b}|F(z)|<\infty$), continuous, and complex-differentiable at every point of $S_b^\circ$, and set $$M_0:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t)|,\qquad M_1:=\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+ib)|.$$ For $0<s<b$, $$\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|F(t+is)|\le M_0^{1-s/b}M_1^{s/b},$$ where each exponent is positive and $0^r=0$ for $r>0$. In particular, if $M_0,M_1\le C$ then $|F(z)|\le C$ on $S_b$. If two bounded continuous functions on $S_b$, holomorphic inside, have the same lower boundary values, then they agree on all of $S_b$.

Fix $d\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Then the factor inclusion $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)=T\otimes I$ is an isometric unital $*$-homomorphism: $$\|\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)\|=\|T\|\qquad(T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda).$$ For nested finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\Lambda''$, the inclusions compose: $\iota_{\Lambda',\Lambda''}\circ\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}=\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda''}$.

Let $H$ be a complex inner-product space of finite dimension $D\geq1$, with inner product linear in its first argument. Every Hermitian endomorphism $M$ has an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues. For a real function $f$ on its finite spectrum, define $f(M)$ by its spectral projections; this definition is independent of the choice of eigenbasis. In particular positive square roots, exponentials, and logarithms on positive supports are well defined. For a density matrix $\rho$ on $H$, meaning a Hermitian positive semidefinite operator with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)=\sum_jp_j\langle Au_j,u_j\rangle$ for bounded $A$, where $\rho=\sum_jp_j|u_j\rangle\langle u_j|$. The weighted form $(X,Y)_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho X^*Y)$ satisfies Cauchy–Schwarz, $|(X,Y)_\rho|^2\leq(X,X)_\rho(Y,Y)_\rho$. Finally, $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^2)\leq1$, with equality exactly for rank-one densities, and those are exactly the extreme points of the finite density-matrix set.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Cauchy-sequence completion. For the local spin system of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], the normed $*$-algebra $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and its completion $\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] are well defined; $\mathcal A$ is a unital complex C*-algebra and $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is norm dense in it. If $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and $B\in\mathcal A_\Delta$ for disjoint finite regions $\Lambda,\Delta$, then $AB=BA$.

Let $\mathcal H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let $H=H^*$ on $\mathcal H$ with energy units J, let $\hbar>0$ have units J s, and let $\beta>0$ have units J$^{-1}$. Write $\operatorname{Tr}$ for the ordinary finite-dimensional trace. Assume the finite spectral-calculus and unital C$^*$-algebra clauses [A1]–[A2] below. Define the finite-matrix Heisenberg group $$\alpha_t^H(X):=e^{itH/\hbar}Xe^{-itH/\hbar}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H),\ t\in\mathbb R).$$ A state $\omega$ on the unital C$^*$-algebra $\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$ satisfies the $\beta$-KMS strip condition of [[def-qsm-kms-state]] for $\alpha^H$ if and only if $$\omega(X)=\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H}X)}{\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H})}\qquad(X\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)).$$ Here $\beta$ has units J$^{-1}$, $H$ has units J, and the physical-time strip has width $\beta\hbar$ seconds. The result is finite-dimensional and makes no infinite-volume or relaxation claim.

Assume Countable Choice and the finite-matrix C*-identity condition [A1] below. Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal A$ be its norm completion as in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. These assumptions give the conditional unital C*-algebra structure supplied by [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. Let $\Phi$ be a uniformly bounded finite-range interaction of [[def-qsm-bounded-finite-range-interaction]]. For any increasing finite exhaustion $\Lambda_n\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$, the free-boundary finite-volume maps $\alpha_t^{\Lambda_n}$ converge in norm on every local observable, uniformly for $t$ in compact intervals. Their limit is independent of the exhaustion and extends uniquely to a strongly continuous one-parameter group $\alpha_t$ of $*$-automorphisms of $\mathcal A$. Strong continuity means $t\mapsto\alpha_t(A)$ is norm-continuous for every fixed $A\in\mathcal A$. This result does not assert that an infinite-volume Hamiltonian is an element of $\mathcal A$ or a bounded operator on a preselected infinite tensor-product Hilbert space.

transitive_in_run_suppliers.interface_excerpt: Let $H=H^*$ be a finite-dimensional Hamiltonian with energy unit J and let $\hbar>0$ have unit J s. For $t\in\mathbb R$, $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ is unitary and $U(t+s)=U(t)U(s)$. For a density $\rho$, the Schrödinger state $U(t)\rho U(t)^*$ and the Heisenberg observable $\alpha_t(A)=U(t)^*AU(t)$ have the same trace expectation, and the von Neumann entropy is unchanged. If $\sigma_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$, $Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}$, then it is stationary and satisfies the finite Gibbs KMS strip identity $ F_{A,B}(t+i\beta\hbar)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta\alpha_t(B)A),\qquad F_{A,B}(z)=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_\beta A\alpha_z(B)), $ where $\alpha_z(B)=e^{izH/\hbar}Be^{-izH/\hbar}$. The function is entire and bounded on $0\leq\operatorname{Im}z\leq\beta\hbar$. No infinite-volume KMS existence or approach to equilibrium follows.

transitive_in_run_suppliers.interface_excerpt: Let $\mathcal A$ be the unital quasi-local spin C*-algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], whose C*-structure uses Countable Choice as in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]].
